items.title: No local measure of compliance or timing
items.whyItMatters: The network relies on anecdote; the retrieved rural service treated only 58 percent of eligible patients (claim c1).
items.opportunity: Measure eligibility, administration and time from injury in ambulance records against the pathway standard.

items.title: Outcomes cannot be linked while the agreement is lapsed
items.whyItMatters: Without hospital data, nothing can be said about whether early treatment helps here, and partial linkage would miss the sickest patients (claim c3).
items.opportunity: Seek renewal of the agreement for all three hospitals before planning any outcome analysis.

items.title: Injury time is often estimated
items.whyItMatters: Timing standards depend on the injury time, which was estimated for almost one in five patients in the retrieved review.
items.opportunity: Record whether injury time was known or estimated and report timing for both groups.

items.title: Older patients and single-crew attendance
items.whyItMatters: Older patients and those attended by one paramedic received the drug less often.
items.opportunity: Report compliance by age group and crew configuration.

errorsFound: The need hopes to show that early treatment improves outcomes; without linked hospital data the network can describe compliance and timing but not effects.
reevaluation: Compliance and timing can be audited now; whether the network should also study outcomes cannot be settled until the data-sharing agreement is renewed.
summary: Four gaps; the missing local measure and the lapsed linkage are high severity.
